## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.6`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noSvelteIgnoredUnsubscribe`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**warning**](/reference/diagnostics#warning).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`svelte`](/linter/domains#svelte)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`svelte/no-ignored-unsubscribe`](https://sveltejs.github.io/eslint-plugin-svelte/rules/no-ignored-unsubscribe/)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noSvelteIgnoredUnsubscribe": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow ignoring the function returned by a store's `subscribe()` method.

Calling `subscribe()` on a Svelte store returns a function that stops the subscription.
If you don't keep this function, you can never stop the subscription: the store keeps
calling your callback and keeps it in memory after you no longer need it. This is a
memory leak.

The rule reports a `subscribe()` call when its result is not used, for example when it
isn't saved in a variable, returned, or passed to another function.

## Examples

### Invalid

```svelte
<script>
import { count } from "./stores.js";

count.subscribe((value) => {
    console.log(value);
});
</script>
```

### Valid

```svelte
<script>
import { onDestroy } from "svelte";
import { count } from "./stores.js";

const unsubscribe = count.subscribe((value) => {
    console.log(value);
});

onDestroy(unsubscribe);
</script>
```
